action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

## 4. Spec problems (with evidence)

**P0. Spec v0 does not specify either contract.** §75: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here." AGENTS.md: "`specs/` is normative and the only source of semantics." Annex D calls itself "non normative" and says "les résultats … concernent le modèle exploratoire …, **pas** automatiquement les règles corrigées". DS-v1 exists only in the brief. Every HandlePool/DataStack definition beyond §36/§37/§56/§58/§89 therefore encodes semantics from outside `specs/`. A decision is needed: either accept Annex D + brief obligation 5 and DS-v1 as the normative source for this formalization (and cite them), or add the contracts to `specs/`.

**P1. Pool slot layout is under-determined, and the choice changes accepted programs.** D.1: "Les slots sont des sous-emplacements deux à deux disjoints, inclus dans `storage`". `newPool(storage, internal)` receives no slot description. The draft picks the direct children (`newPoolEff` HP:116). Example: storage `S = {a: {x, y}, b}`. "Slots = children" gives 2 slots `a, b`, so a third `allocSlot` gives `fail`. "Slots = leaves" gives 3 slots `x, y, b`, so the third gives `ok`. A storage that is a single leaf gives 0 slots under the draft, so every `allocSlot` gives `fail`.

**P2. Outcome of `freeSlot` on a free slot whose generation matches.** D.3: "un slot déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité" says it must not succeed, but not whether it gives `fail` or `reject`. Example (`pool_free_entry_handle` HZ:977): on a fresh pool, the fabricated handle `⟨0,0,0⟩` names free slot 0 of generation 0. The draft gives `ok`. The contract excludes `ok`, but `fail` (like `resolve`'s "slot … libre ⇒ fail") and `reject` are both possible readings.

**P3. `resolve`: `reject` (no right) vs `fail` (bad handle) when both hold.** The right in D.2 ("exercice légal de `internal` au mode requis") includes the effective mode, which depends on the state. Spec v0 §77 orders the arena's analogous checks as availability `fail` (77.4) **before** the effective-right `reject` (77.5). Jalon3 H31a ("Deux `resolve Modify` simultanés, **quels que soient les handles** : le second `reject`") and the draft (HZ:590, `ResolveStep 0 ⟨0, 1, 7⟩ .modify h31 .reject` with a stale generation 7) put `reject` first. Example: with an active `Modify` companion, `resolve(stale h, Modify)` gives `reject` in the draft and `fail` under the §77 analogy. §58 defers to "the operation's contract", which does not settle it.

**P4. Scope of "excluding `internal` and its ancestors" in `freeSlot`.**
- (a) D.3 lists only "aucune dépendance utilisable ne serait invalidée, aucune feuille n'est épinglée, et aucune autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres"; the brief says "preconditions excluding internal and its ancestors". O12.3 includes "No place remaining usable after the effect depends on an authority held by `place`, **its root**, …". Example: a pool whose `internal` is the storage root (the `pb` setup HZ:565). If some usable place carries `internal` in `D` through `depend` (O5), the literal O12.3 rejects `freeSlot` (draft `EndUseAnchorOK` MM03:3989, `¬ IsRootOf`), although `freeSlot` leaves `internal` active. Whether the exemption also covers O12.3's root clause is not stated.
- (b) Kernel side, for the kernel mapper: in O12.2, "No active descendant over the leaves of `place` … is held outside the places dying with `place`, in a way that would prevent rights from returning", the descendant has no stated referent. The draft's literal reading (`EndUseAccessOK` MM03:3979: every active derived authority on an ending leaf) forbids `endUse` of any value stored inside an issued arena block while the block authority, held by the destination outside the block, is active. That authority is the one through which O12.1's `Modify` is exercised. Witness: `pool_freeSlot_derived_internal` HZ:925. It decides whether `freeSlot` can be a kernel `endUse` step (§2 item 8).

**P5. D.3 contradicts itself when `dst` lies in the allocated slot.** "Le contenu du slot demeure `Uninit` … l'écriture du handle dans `dst` n'initialise pas le slot" holds only if `dst` lies outside the slot. Unlike O18.2 ("leaf `destination` is not in `region`"), `allocSlot` does not exclude it. Example: a frame with `Modify` on the pool value has `internal` exercisable (§43, holder chain), so it has `HasRight .modify q` for a free-slot leaf `q`. `allocSlot(pool, dst := q)` satisfies every D.3 precondition (usable leaf, not `Init`, no authority held), picks slot `q`, and writes the handle into it: the slot becomes `Init`.

**P6. "Les entrées libres sont `Uninit`" (D.1) is not an invariant of the open model.** A frame with `Modify` on the pool value can `derive` from `internal` onto a free slot (O1) and `write3` it (O10). That is the same mechanism as the draft counterexample `pool_inv_not_preserved` HP:1830 (a derive from the companion onto a free entry). A later `allocSlot` then hands out an `Init` slot even if `newPool` required `Uninit` storage. D.4 assigns encapsulation to Spec 9. The property can be stated only as an `allocSlot`/`freeSlot` effect, not as a reachable-state theorem, unless Spec 9 encapsulation is modeled.

**P7. DataStack "a cell above m" is undefined.** It could mean `[m.top, top)` (cells that `rewind` returns) or any index ≥ `m.top`. Example (draft `opsE8`, `case_rewind_reading` DSL:1013): after an intermediate `rewind`, an authority `9` derived from `internal` covers cell 3 above the current top. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is accepted by the draft; under the literal "covers a cell above m" it is rejected. Safety is the same either way, since the next `push` of cell 3 is rejected by the effective right (§43 case 3). A "region issued after m" reading (Derivability (f) 7) gives a third answer for grown blocks (`opsE4`).

**P8. DataStack ordering of statics against `fail`.** §58 says statics come before dynamic availability "according to the operation's contract". DS-v1 (as quoted) does not order (i) `rewind`'s administrative right (§36) against the dead/foreign-mark `fail`, or (ii) `push`/`grow` statics against the no-room `fail`. §75 describes the derived issue as "split followed by store (after checking availability)", which suggests availability first. §77 puts statics first. Example: a callee with no right over the stack value (`opsZ` DSL:1029) calls `rewind` with a removed mark. The draft gives `fail`; statics first gives `reject`.

**P9. DataStack `grow` details not covered by DS-v1 (as quoted):**
- `extra = 0`: the draft gives `reject` (DSL:221 `0 < extra`).
- whether `b` must be releasable (the draft checks `ReleasePre` statically);
- the destination after the block value has been transferred: the draft stores into the recorded `Blk.dst`, which may then be `Moved` and no longer the holder (Derivability (f)).

**P10 (low). `resolveMany Observe` with invalid handles.** D.2 states the atomic `fail` ("toute identité invalide, génération périmée, entrée libre ou répétition de slot donne `fail` **atomique**") only in the `Modify` sentence. For `Observe`, it says only "sans `split` ni contrôle de distinction". The natural reading (an invalid handle gives an atomic `fail`) is not written down.

No contradiction with the Charter was found. Charter §4.1 lists the five guarantees and §3.4 sends features to libraries; both are consistent with every item above.

---

## 5. Representation choices recommended (they change no accepted program)

- **R1.** One library record `Lib` (arenas, pools, stacks, `nextPool`, `nextMark`, ghost `res`) beside `S3`, with a single function `liveInternals : Lib → S3 → List AuthorityId` for §56. This follows §38 and §56 ("Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel").
- **R2.** Pool identity as a counter (`nId`), mark identity as a counter (`fresh`): §9 "A monotonically increasing counter is one possible representation".
- **R3.** A stack's identity is its registry index; stacks are never removed, so indices are never reused. `Mark = (stack, id, top)` as in the draft.
- **R4.** Ghost resolution registry `Res` (companion, mode, entries tagged with slot and generation), read only by `unresolve` and by the invariants. It is auxiliary information that creates no rights (§38 last sentence, applied to library state).
- **R5.** `resolveMany Modify` realized as `derive` companion + `split` on the entry footprints. With the distinctness check placed first, this accepts exactly the batches that successive `derive`s from the companion would accept, because entries are disjoint (`pool_entries_disjoint`).
- **R6.** Library operations as relations with `ok | fail | reject` (`POutcome`/`Out`), `fail` carrying the unchanged state. `allocSlot` is a relation over any free slot. Executable runners (`pexec`, `drun`) keep a deterministic choice (`firstFree`) and are proven to agree with the relation on every result they return (DESIGN.md, Representation).
- **R7.** Stack availability as the index `top`, with `available st := st.cells.drop st.top`. This is equivalent to an explicit leaf set (§46 `available: Set<Leaf>`) because `push` and `grow` take cells only at the top and `rewind` returns exactly `[m.top, top)`. A lemma stating that equivalence makes C5 literal.
- **R8.** Handle as `(poolId, slot index, gen)` with the slot index read as a position in `Pool.slots`; a slot index out of range never names an entry (`fail`).
- **R9.** `AdminRight` (§2 item 3) shared by arenas, pools and stacks, so one definition carries the §36 citation.

90	## 2. Required changes (ordered), each with its clause and proof impact
91	
92	Infrastructure comes first, because every later change depends on it.
93	
94	1. **One library state outside `S3`** (§38, §46, §47; enables §56). Remove `arenas` from the kernel state (a kernel-scope change, coordinate with the kernel/arena mappers). Introduce `Lib := {arenas, pools, stacks, nextPool, nextMark, res (ghost)}` and a single library step that contains kernel steps and the arena, pool and stack operations.
95	   *Impact:* `PStep` HP:336, `PReach` HP:354, `kstep_keeps`/`step_keeps` HP:392/451, `step_fp` HP:515, `reachable_step` HP:530, `pstep_steps` HP:647, `pReach_reachable` HP:678, `pReach_inv` HP:1234, `dexec`/`dexec_reach`/`drun_reach` DSL:254/412/429 change type. The arena cases (`newArena`, `issue`, `reset`) move from `Step` to library steps. Their `KeepsAuth`/`FpStable` arguments are unchanged in substance. `KGuard` DSL:246 disappears into the library `newArena`. Every executable case (`pexec`, `drun`, `HZ` runs) must be re-run.
96	2. **Unified §56 guard** `LiveInternalFree L s i := ∀ admin ∈ arenas ∪ pools ∪ stacks, Active admin.internal → admin.internal ≠ i`, used by `newArena`, `newPool` and `newStack` (§56 ¶1, §76.4, D.1).
97	   *Impact:* none on safety theorems (§56 ¶2; `pinv_newPool` HP:1004 uses only `hu` and `hint`). Witnesses `pool_two_on_one_internal`, `pool_two_freeSlot_cross`, `arena_on_pool_internal` (HZ:953–975) and the `newArena` conjunct of `case_stacks` DSL:962 now give `reject`.

# Readings — key `machine` (formal/Ern/MemoryModel/Machine.lean, spec v0 §8–§20)

Format: clause, quote, reading used, alternative, example whose verdict changes. "Representation" = changes no accepted program.

## Spec problems

**S1. §15.3 (bytes "required").** Quote: "the bytes **required** for the representation being read are initialized". §15 ¶5 makes 4, 6, 7 parametric, so 3 should be concrete, but which bytes are "required" depends on the read type's representation, which §10 ¶6 defers ("Constraints on invalid representations, padding bytes, and type alignment will be specified by the corresponding specifications").
Reading used (brief): every byte of the accessed range (`Alloc.InitRange (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len` inside `CanRead`).
Alternative: a type-dependent required-byte set, as a parameter like 4, 6, 7.
Example: raw typed read of a 2-byte representation whose second byte is padding and was never written: `ub` under the reading used, `ok` under the alternative (other conditions holding).

**S2. Byte read vs typed read (§20.2 ¶1, §16 ¶5, §18 ¶1).** Quotes: §20.2 ¶1 "A valid **byte read** does not modify memory state … A raw typed read must **additionally** satisfy type, alignment, and concurrency obligations"; §16 ¶5 "every valid raw byte read of a subrange …"; §18 ¶1 "A data race is UB". No clause lists the conditions of a byte read.
Reading used: one read relation `ReadStep` (typed, with type argument and obligations `ObR`). A byte read is an instance under a context that fixes its obligations. `write_read_sub` and `write_noninterference` quantify over every obligation spec `R` and every type, so they hold whichever way S2 is decided.
Alternative: a separate `ByteRead` relation without §15.4/§15.6/§15.7.
Example: a raw byte read of byte `x` concurrent with an unordered non-atomic write to `x`: `ok` in the machine under the alternative (byte read has no concurrency obligation), UB under §18.

**S3. §16 ¶3 presupposes a counter (minor).** Quote: "allocation identity and the allocation counter are unaffected", against §9 ¶7 "A monotonically increasing counter is one possible representation, not a language requirement" and §9 ¶12. Formalized with the counter (`WriteStep_frame`: `s'.next = s.next`). Does not block.

## Reading decisions

**R1. Totality form (§20.1 ¶3).** Quote: "Memory-machine relations may be deterministic and mathematically total even when certain obligations are not constructively decidable. A classical proof of totality is not a runtime requirement." The axiom policy of this pass excludes `Classical.choice`, and `∃ o, ReadStep … o` on every state is equivalent to excluded middle on `stat` (resp. `C`, `AllocPre`).
Used: `ReadStep_total` … `AllocStep_total` state `¬¬ ∃ o, …` on every state (constructive, classically equivalent to `∃`), and `*_total_on` state `∃ o` on the interpreter domain (stat proof given, `DecidableRel C`, `WF s`).
Alternative: `∃ o` on every state via `Classical.em` (one line each, axiom `Classical.choice`). Statement form only; no verdict changes.

**R2. Read/write type (§15.4, §15.6, §16.4, §16.5, §20.3 ¶3).** Representation: opaque `Ty : Type`; `ReadStep ObR ac t s o`, `WriteStep ObW ac t w s o`, `Op.read ac t`, `Op.write ac t w`; obligations `dec`/`stat : State → Access → Ty → …`. No structure assumed on `Ty`. (Draft had no type: a `u32` read and a `[u8;4]` read at the same odd address could not get different outcomes.)

**R3. Resolution (§11 ¶2).** Quote: "a means of access produces a place **only if** provenance identifies a registered allocation (live or dead) and the address range is spatially contained within it". Used: `Access.toPlace` defined exactly when registered ∧ `Spatial` ("iff"). Alternative: a resolution defined on fewer accesses. No relation uses `toPlace`, so no verdict changes (representation).

**R4. Freshness and identity assignment (§9 ¶7, §9 ¶11, §13 ¶1).** Representation: counter `next`, `WF s := ∀ i ≥ next, unregistered`; the machine assigns `s.next`; the "fresh identity" precondition of §9 ¶11 is `s.allocs s.next = none` (dead allocations stay registered, so unregistered = never assigned). Alternative: client-supplied identity with a "never assigned" precondition. No verdict changes on admissible states (`WF` makes the precondition true). Outside the domain `AllocStep` may be `ok` on a non-`WF` state, as §9 ¶10 allows.

**R5. "Absence of an intervening write or invalidation" (§16 ¶5).** Used (`Op.KeepsAlloc`): every intervening operation is a read, a creation, a deallocation of another identity, or a write through another provenance. Alternative: no intervening write at all. The hypothesis used is weaker, so `write_read_sub` is stronger; no verdict changes. `ops = []` gives the immediately following read.

**R6. Non-interference ranges (§16 ¶5).** Quote: "nor that of a range disjoint from the written range". Used: absolute half-open address ranges `[ac.addr, ac.addr + ac.len)` and `[ac'.addr, ac'.addr + ac'.len)` disjoint (`RangeDisjoint`, §9 ¶3); "result of a valid read" compared for `ok` reads before and after with the same obligations and type. The theorem also proves `CanRead s' ac' ↔ CanRead s ac'`.

**R7. Deallocation designation (§17).** Representation: by identity `id` (the provenance of the presenting access) plus presented authority `auth : Nat`; recorded token `freeAuth : Option Nat`; compatibility `C : Nat → Nat → Prop` a context parameter with no decision instance in the relation. §17 states no "address = base" condition.

**R8. Interpreter domains (brief: "static obligations and the admissible-state hypothesis as proof arguments"; obligation 1: "static obligations and WF").** Used: `read`/`write` take the `stat` proof; `alloc` takes `WF s` only (what `AllocPreDec ↔ AllocPre` needs); `dealloc` takes `[DecidableRel C]` and no proof. Agreement is proved on these domains, which contain the admissible states. Alternative: `Admissible s` on every interpreter (smaller domain). No verdict changes.

**R9. Executions (§9 ¶9, §20.1 ¶2 b3, §20.3 ¶3).** Representation: `Exec C ObR ObW ops s₀ s`, a list of `ok` steps under one context; a read step leaves the state unchanged; a `ub` step supplies no state and never occurs inside an execution. `Reachable s₀ s := ∃ ops, Exec … ops s₀ s`; admissibility of `s₀` is a hypothesis of the theorems (`Exec.admissible`), not part of `Reachable`.

**R10. Restrictive derivation subrange (§14 ¶1 b2).** Used: `ac.addr ≤ ac'.addr ∧ ac'.addr + ac'.len ≤ ac.addr + ac.len` (same arithmetic as §15 ¶1). A zero-length derivative at the source's end address counts as a subrange. Alternative: require `ac'.addr < ac.addr + ac.len` for zero length. `Derive` is used by no relation (formation has no transition, §14 ¶4), so no machine verdict changes.

**R11. Written representation.** Representation: `w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat`, only positions `[0, len)` used; a list would add a length-mismatch case that no clause classifies.

**R12. Citation numbering.** Paragraphs counted with a list belonging to the paragraph that introduces it. The frame clause "Bytes in other allocations …" is cited §16 ¶3 (the brief writes §16 ¶4, which under this count is "Conditions 4, 5, and 6 …").

## Design note (formal/DESIGN.md, not decided here)

DESIGN.md "Representation": "Semantics is a step function where the spec is deterministic". Spec §20.1 ¶1: "Raw memory-model operations are interpreted by **transition relations**", and a total step function would need a classical decision of `stat`. The module follows the spec (relations + computable interpreters + agreement). DESIGN.md also asks for fuel interpreters over sequences; none is provided here (not in the brief).

# Annexe D — Instance `HandlePool` (non normative, contrat de bibliothèque)

Cette annexe décrit une **instance de bibliothèque** de la discipline MM-03, et non une nouvelle opération primitive du langage. Les noms sont sémantiques. Le contrat doit être reconstruit et vérifié ; les résultats du jalon 3 concernent le modèle exploratoire et ses conditions, **pas** automatiquement les règles corrigées ci-dessous.

## D.1 — Identité, état et stockage

Un handle est une donnée `(poolId, slot, gen)` **sans autorité d'accès intrinsèque**. L'identité logique `poolId` est fraîche et n'est pas réutilisée pendant l'exécution pertinente : détruire puis recréer un pool à la même adresse ne réactive pas un ancien handle. Chaque pool vivant conserve une entrée abstraite `{storage, internal, slots}`, où chaque slot possède `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}`. Les slots sont des sous-emplacements deux à deux disjoints, inclus dans `storage` ; leur métadonnée abstraite est représentée en octets par l'implémentation de bibliothèque.

`storage` peut être local, statique, alloué ou être un bloc issu d'une arène. **`newPool(storage, internal)` exige que toutes les feuilles du stockage d'entrée soient `Uninit`** et doit vérifier la garde unifiée de MM-03.3 §2.7 bis sur les deux registres des abstractions vivantes. Il reprend les autres obligations applicables de `newArena` sans fabriquer ni droits ni initialisation des valeurs de slots. Les entrées libres sont `Uninit` ; leur génération initiale est zéro. Une autorité ne peut être `internal` de deux abstractions vivantes, et une arène ne peut réutiliser l'`internal` d'un pool vivant.

## D.2 — Emprunt composé et résolution

Une résolution réussie dérive **de `internal` une autorité compagne** couvrant toutes les feuilles du stockage du pool, de mode `Observe` ou `Modify`, puis dérive **de cette compagne** une autorité de même mode par entrée résolue. L'autorité d'entrée est une descendante de la compagne, et non une autre dérivation indépendante de `internal`. Les deux sont soumises aux règles ordinaires de modes effectifs, d'exercice, de détention, d'ancrage et de transfert ; aucune permission nouvelle n'est créée.

`resolve(h, Observe | Modify)` vérifie l'identité de pool, la génération et la vivacité du slot **avant toute création d'autorité** : handle d'un autre pool, périmé, slot absent ou libre ⇒ `fail`, sans changement d'état. Une résolution valide exige l'exercice légal de `internal` au mode requis. Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles compagnes sur l'intégralité du stockage du pool ; des compagnes `Observe` peuvent coexister. Il est impossible de libérer une compagne tant que ses descendantes d'entrée sont actives (O3.2). La propriété d'exclusivité concerne toutes les suites d'opérations admises du noyau, pas seulement deux appels successifs de `resolve`.

`resolveMany(handles, Modify)` crée **une** compagne `Modify` et une autorité `Modify` par entrée. La distinction des slots est vérifiée dynamiquement pour ce lot ; toute identité invalide, génération périmée, entrée libre ou répétition de slot donne `fail` **atomique**, sans création partielle de droits. `resolveMany(handles, Observe)` utilise des dérivations `Observe` de la compagne `Observe`, **sans `split` ni contrôle de distinction** : la répétition du même handle valide est permise. Les `reject` de discipline d'accès restent distincts des `fail` de validation des handles.

`unresolve` libère d'abord toutes les dérivées d'entrée encore actives, puis la compagne. Les règles de `release`, y compris celles qui empêchent la libération en présence de descendants ou d'ancres valides, restent applicables ; le contrat ne supprime pas silencieusement des autorités transférées.

## D.3 — Allocation et fin d'usage de slot

`allocSlot(pool, dst)` exige un pool vivant, l'autorisation d'administration de ses métadonnées, une destination utilisable et libre d'autorité active, non `Init`, apte à recevoir la représentation d'un handle. `fail` si aucun slot libre ; `ok` choisit un slot libre, le rend vivant, conserve sa génération et écrit son handle dans la seule feuille `dst`, selon les obligations de représentation (Spec 4) et d'ABI (Spec 11). **Le contenu du slot demeure `Uninit`** jusqu'à son écriture ; l'écriture du handle dans `dst` n'initialise pas le slot.

`freeSlot(h)` exige un pool **vivant** et `MetaRight`, c'est-à-dire le droit légal d'administration de la valeur pool par `Modify` exerçable ou par mutation `writeShared` admissible de ses métadonnées `SharedMutable`. `fail` si l'identité ou la génération ne correspond pas ; un slot déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité. Pour réussir, la fin logique du contenu doit être admissible : **aucune dépendance utilisable** ne serait invalidée, **aucune feuille n'est épinglée**, et **aucune autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres**. En particulier, aucune descendante active d'une compagne ne doit subsister sur cette entrée. Le contrôle n'interprète pas `internal` comme un emprunt externe empêchant systématiquement le nettoyage de ses propres slots.

L'effet `ok` applique au **contenu** les effets de fin d'usage d'`endUse`, remet les feuilles de l'entrée à `Uninit`, marque l'entrée libre et incrémente sa génération ; **il ne désalloue pas implicitement l'allocation MM-02 du stockage**. Il ne s'agit pas de supposer une invocation de O12 autorisée par simple `MetaRight` : la correspondance des effets et la préservation des invariants sous ce droit constituent une **obligation explicite de reconstruction**, notamment dans les cas `writeShared`.

## D.4 — Invariant corrigé et limites

`PoolInv` exige : (1) les entrées sont deux à deux disjointes et incluses dans le stockage ; (2) aucune autorité d'entrée active ne désigne un slot libre ou une ancienne génération (`pool_no_stale_access`) ; (3) **garantie de transition** : `freeSlot` n'aboutit jamais si une descendante active d'une compagne couvre le slot concerné. La dernière clause concerne le succès des transitions, non une interdiction globale de toutes les dérivations du noyau sur des slots libres. Les dérivations ordinaires issues d'une autorité d'entrée restent permises par le noyau.

Les générations sont des entiers naturels dans le modèle abstrait. Leur débordement ou leur recyclage dans une représentation finie doivent être empêchés par l'implémentation (par exemple retrait définitif d'un slot) ; l'ABI est spécifiée en Spec 11. L'encapsulation qui empêche un client d'accéder directement à une compagne administrative appartient à la Spec 9. Les handles persistants peuvent représenter des liens cycliques ; les résolutions qui en découlent restent temporaires et soumises à MM-03.

**Statut des preuves :** le jalon 3 rapporte `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive`, `pool_no_stale_access`, `pool_resolveMany_atomic`, `pool_resolveMany_distinct`, `pool_freeSlot_ends_content` et `pool_entries_disjoint` sur son brouillon, sous les hypothèses détaillées dans `J3_v0.1.md`. Il rapporte également un contre-exemple à l'ancienne formulation de `pool_inv_preserved`. **Il ne constitue pas encore la preuve** de la nouvelle règle `freeSlot` sous `MetaRight` ni de la totalité du contrat corrigé : ces obligations sont consignées en annexe F.

# Annexe E — Registre inter-spécifications (non normatif pour la Spec 1)

| Destination | Obligations ouvertes ou précisées |
|---|---|
| **Spec 2 — Concurrence** | Partie concurrente de `stat` ; `writeShared` et synchronisation ; transférabilité, partageabilité, suspension concurrente ; cas H39, H41. |
| **Spec 3 — Contrôle de flux et appels** | Protection forte de paramètres (`Reach`, `lineage`, `derivedIn`, G1', A3 strict) ; ré-emprunt d'un paramètre `Modify` par un paramètre dérivé `Observe` (H01, admis dans le noyau séquentiel, sans promettre la protection forte) ; **passage par valeur (`sink`) vers l'appelé** : prévoir la primitive MM-03 correspondante, transfert d'un emplacement de l'appelant vers un local de l'appelé au moment de l'entrée, sans affaiblir arbitrairement O4 ; retour et `defer` (H16, H27b, H38, H40, H42). |
| **Spec 4 — Types** | Validité de représentation (`dec`), `SameSizeAlong`, information de forme pour des régions non contiguës, feuille de destination d'une référence typée, correspondance `kind` et type ; **mémoire rendue par une abstraction de réutilisation (bloc d'arène réémis, entrée de pool) exposée comme typée non initialisée jusqu'à écriture explicite**, sans réinterprétation implicite d'anciens octets. La décision ne change pas rétroactivement les effets d'initialisation de `reset` sur l'état abstrait MM-03. |
| **Spec 9 — Encapsulation** | Empêcher l'usage extérieur des autorités internes/compagnes administratives des bibliothèques sûres. |
| **Spec 11 — ABI** | Alignement (`dec`), taille/encodage et décodage des références et handles, largeur des adresses, espace fini et épuisement, générations bornées, placement et jetons (`PlacementOK`, `TokCompat`). |
| **Spec 13 — Compilateur** | Justification du lowering de `noalias` au-delà de l'exclusivité du noyau. |
| **Spécification des ressources** | Obligations de libération attachées à certains types (H43). |
| **Bibliothèques** | `DeclaredDisjoint` par disjonction réelle des feuilles ; `FreeCompat`, représentation et atomicité des métadonnées d'arène/pool, garantie unifiée des registres `internal`, contrat `MetaRight` et fin de slot. |

# Annexe F — Registre de reconstruction de référence (non normatif)

La reconstruction de référence doit repartir du texte **validé**, et non des approximations du brouillon. Les éléments suivants ne sont pas tous prouvés à ce stade :

1. **Six écarts du brouillon MM-03** (`MM23_v0.1.md`, section (f)) : (i) feuilles lues/écrites utilisables, (ii) empreintes composées uniquement de feuilles, (iii) `alloc` créant une racine unique, (iv) marques de mort transitives après `free` et `endUse`, (v) `RootLive`/`RootHeld`, (vi) bonne fondation des chaînes de possession.

## 36. Shared Mutation and Internal Administration

An abstraction may keep its metadata in `SharedMutable` storage and modify it through `writeShared` to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts. **Shared mutation of metadata does not, however, grant the right to create, recycle, or terminate exclusive authority over the administered storage.** Such operations require `internal` to be exercisable in `Modify` mode from the value administering the storage.

For every administrative abstraction, including arenas, `HandlePool`, and `DataStack`, **`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the administering value**. The `writeShared` branch alone is insufficient. Operations issuing, recycling, ending, or invalidating regions must preserve active authorities and dependencies. Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations: any synchronized implementation of it belongs to Spec 2. These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel.

## 37. Dependent Values and Persistent References

When a value depends on the validity of other storage, that dependency must be carried by an explicit mechanism. In particular, this model retains:

- joint ownership or legal transfer of the resource;
- **non-escaping** dependent values, governed by `depend`, `store`, `AnchorOrder`, and end-of-use operations; they may survive a call if their anchors come from still-valid caller resources;
- library handles checked for identity and generation upon resolution, which are not authorities by themselves;
- validity durations bound to a frame or context, without a universal system of first-class lifetimes;
- safe abstractions encapsulating, when necessary, unsafe operations and proofs of their obligations.

**Not adopted as a universal ERN mechanism:** a first-class persistent reference subject to general lifetime constraints at the type-system level. The above mechanisms are complementary; neither a handle nor a temporary access guarantees the perpetual validity of its target resource on its own.

# VI. Abstract Authority Machine

The components described below constitute the logical state of the sequential discipline. They prescribe neither generalized runtime metadata nor reference syntax.

## 38. Machine State

The access discipline is based on the finite state

\[ S_3=(F,P,I,A,D) \]

where `F` represents the frame stack, `P` the places, `I` their initialization, `A` the authorities, and `D` the validity anchors. Administrative states of arenas and other library abstractions are separate from `S₃`. The external contract `K` is a separate parameter. The internal representation may carry auxiliary information that creates no new rights.

## 39. Execution Frames

`F` is a nonempty stack of identified, non-duplicate frames. Every frame except the initial frame knows its parent. Frames hold temporary authorities and directly local places. The **current frame** is at the top of the stack. `ancestor(f₁, f₂)` means `f₁` is `f₂` or an ancestor of `f₂` in the stack and its call chain.

The base frame, whose identity is 0 in states reachable from the initial state, never exits. An exited frame can neither be the terminal owner of a usable place nor hold an authority that remains active. Frames have semantic existence; no particular runtime representation is required.

## 40. Logical Places, Leaves, and Ownership

A place has an identity, optionally a structural parent, an abstract `kind`, an owner `owner : Frame | Place`, and a logical death marker. Structural parenthood `partOf(p,q)` describes the subplaces of a value; `owner` describes **who keeps the storage** of a root place valid. An owned place may lie outside its owner's direct footprint; ownership and composition are therefore distinct.

A **leaf** is a place with no structural children. `footprint(p)` contains the leaves of `p`, and access rights over a place are evaluated on those leaves. Places transitively owned by a value are not automatically leaves of its `footprint`. A logical unit of the access discipline does not automatically constitute an additional allocation in the elementary memory machine.

A place `p` is **usable** (`Usable(s,p)`) if and only if:

1. `p` exists and is not marked dead;
2. if its owner is a frame, that frame belongs to the stack;
3. if its owner is a place `q`, then `q` is itself usable and the chain terminates at a frame in the stack.

An ownership cycle makes no place usable. `placeFrame(p)` is the terminal frame of this chain when `p` is usable. Structural parts share their parent's owner and death marker. A value may be logically ended by `endUse` without the place that contained it becoming unusable; the substorages it owned may, however, die.

A **root place** has no structural parent. Every root place has a root authority of own mode `Modify`, with no origin, held exactly by that place's owner (`RootHeld`). This authority cannot be transferred in isolation; root ownership follows a legal transfer of the owning value when necessary.

## 41. Leaf Initialization States

Every tracked leaf has exactly one of the states `Uninit`, `Init`, or `Moved`.

- `Uninit`: no initialized value available in this leaf.
- `Init`: initialized value, subject to type, representation, and storage obligations.
- `Moved`: value consumed by transfer, inaccessible as its former value.

Aggregates may be partially initialized. Both `Uninit` and `Moved` prohibit ordinary reads, while remaining distinct states for diagnostics and end-of-use obligations. An initialization state creates no access permission.

## 42. Authorities, Modes, Holders, and Origins

An authority conceptually has the following fields:

```text
Authority {
    id
    mode: Observe | Modify
    origin?: AuthorityId
    footprint: Set<Leaf>
    holder: Frame | Place
    active: Bool
}
```

`origin` links a derived authority to its current origin. Authorities have fresh identities and well-formed origin chains. A root authority has no origin; a derived authority has one. Creating derived rights does not increase the scope or permitted mode of the origin.

The **holder** (`holder`) is not the **owner** (`owner`). An authority derived by `derive` or `split` is initially held by the current frame; `store` or a permitted transfer may make it held by a place. The derived `issue` operation proceeds through `split` followed by `store`. `release` does not release a root. There is no persistent `Suspended` field: suspension of rights is inferred from active descendants and applies leaf by leaf.

## 43. Effective Rights and Exercise of Authorities

For an authority `a` and a leaf `l`, `effective(s,a,l)` is derived from the active descendants of `a` whose footprint contains `l`:

1. if `a` is inactive or does not cover `l`, its effective mode is absent;
2. if no active descendant covers `l`, the effective mode is the own mode of `a`;
3. if an active descendant with own mode `Modify` covers `l`, the effective mode of `a` is absent;
4. otherwise, when the covering active descendants are `Observe`, the effective mode of `a` on `l` is `Observe`.

The effect is **local to each leaf**: after splitting a region, the origin may retain effective `Modify` over undistributed leaves.

Requested modes are ordered `Observe ≤ Modify`. `ExercisableAt(s,a,m)` means:

- `a` is active and its own mode permits `m`;
- either `a` is held by the current frame;
- or `a` is held by a place `p`, and the current frame has, over **all** leaves of `p`, an authority itself exercisable in mode `m` with sufficient effective mode.

The latter clause is recursive along the holder chain. Thus, being active or covering a leaf does not automatically make an authority exercisable. `HasRight(s,m,p)` means the current frame has exercise in mode `m` and sufficient effective mode **over every leaf in `p`'s footprint**. Every operation requires the modes it actually needs; an authority's own mode alone is insufficient.

## 44. Dependencies and Effective Anchors

`D(p)` is the set of authorities serving as **validity anchors** for place `p`. An anchor is valid as long as the authority it names is active. Dependencies of contained values are accounted for transitively. Relevant dependencies follow the value during transfer; those of its container do not automatically follow a part transferred in isolation.

For an authority `x`, its **effective anchor** is the root reached by traversing its origin chain. It does not necessarily coincide with its current holder. Lifetime constraints are calculated from the frame of that effective anchor and the frames of places that remain usable. A dependency cannot create a right or artificially extend a lifetime.

`AnchorOrder` requires, for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, that the frame of the effective anchor of `x` be the frame of `q` or one of its ancestors. `AnchorOrderHeld` imposes the same rule on every **active authority held** by `q`. These conditions apply to the resulting states of operations that move or create holder relations.

## 45. Parameters, Returns, and Reanchoring

A call parameter is an **active derived authority held by the caller** before being passed to the callee; its original provenance may go back to an earlier frame. This interpretation does not require that the authority was originally derived in the calling frame; that additional requirement belongs to Spec 3. The caller **yields** the authority to the new frame: it does not simultaneously retain a copy. If the authority remains in that frame upon return, `exitFrame` releases it; **it is not automatically returned to the caller**. To retain its own right, the caller may pass a **fresh derivative** of the authority it wishes to keep: this is ordinary reborrowing. The definition of ergonomic calling conventions is deferred to Spec 3.

A result is returned by a legal `transfer` into the result place provided by the caller as a `Modify` parameter. Surviving authorities and their dependencies are reanchored by `exitFrame` to still-valid origins. There is no standalone correspondence `M` and no implicit escape permission.

## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.

## 47. Initial State

The kernel's initial state contains only base frame 0 and the declared static storage. Every static leaf has its declared initial state, `Init` or `Uninit`. The roots of static places directly owned by frame 0 have a root `Modify` authority held by that frame; a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter. The initial state invents no dynamic allocation, derived authority, or implicit anchor. The initial arena registry belongs to library state and is empty. The initial frame does not exit.

## 48. External Parametric Contract

`K` contains the predicates `DeclaredDisjoint`, `SharedMutable`, `Pinned`, `ExternalDone`, `Deallocable`, `FreeCompat`, and `Satisfiable`. Their obligations are specified in Section 80. `K` can neither fabricate access rights nor remove an obligation of the Charter. The predicate `Invalidates` is not part of this contract.

# VII. Invariants of Reachable States

Machine states are subject to structural, validity, and exclusivity requirements preserved by permitted transitions under their declared external contracts.

## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

## 50. I1 — Structural Exclusivity

For two active authorities **unrelated by derivation** covering the same leaf, their own modes must both be `Observe`. This rule also applies to leaves identified as `SharedMutable`; their particular mutation is governed by the `writeShared` contract and creates no exception to I1.

Exclusivity of **effective** modes (`effective_exclusive`) is a consequence of I1 and the definition of `effective`, not the definition of I1. On a leaf, two incompatible authorities cannot simultaneously possess incompatible effective rights. The only permitted independent ordinary coexistence is `Observe` / `Observe`.

## 51. I2 — Conservation of Rights

A derived authority covers only a subfootprint of what its origin chain permits and does not elevate its mode. Derivation and splitting restrictions do not allow duplication of an exclusive right over a leaf. Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules. Partial suspension follows from `effective`.

## 52. I3 — Validity of Anchors and Dependencies

Every explicit anchor of a still-usable place is valid. An operation cannot invalidate an anchor retained by a place that remains usable. Transitive propagation of dependencies from contained values does not change this obligation. Dependencies are not permissions and are insufficient to justify an access.

## 53. I4 — Consumption and Movement

A `Moved` leaf cannot be read as if it still contained its previous value. Moving a value does not preserve two copies of an exclusive authority. Initialization state and authority-exercise state are separate checks.

## 54. Anchor Ordering and Absence of Orphan Rights

`AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` are defined in Section 44. `NoDangling` prohibits an **active** authority from covering a leaf belonging to an unusable place; the invariant does not say that a leaf is initialized. `NoOrphan` requires every active authority held by a place to be connected to a frame in the stack through a **finite, non-repeating chain** of authorities: the first link is held by a live frame, and each active link **structurally covers the entirety** of the place holding the next link. The link need not have an effective mode over that place. `NoOrphan` guarantees neither the exercisability of all stored authorities nor freedom from blocking.

## 55. ArenaInv — Invariant of the Arena Abstraction

`ArenaInv` is an invariant of the **library contract**, not an additional predicate of kernel state. For every live arena:

- `storage` designates an existing, usable place; the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`;
- `internal` is active, with own mode `Modify`, held by the arena value;
- available leaves and issued regions belong to the administered storage;
- two still-active issuances have disjoint regions; no leaf of a still-issued region simultaneously belongs to `available`;
- every still-issued block authority is a derivative of `internal` complying with exclusivity and validity rules;
- anchor and ownership restrictions are respected.

Arena entries do not, by themselves, constitute an additional storage owner. Two live arenas may cover common leaves when their `internal` authorities are distinct and their effective rights are compatible; no **global** disjointness of arena footprints is imposed.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.

# VIII. Definition of Transitions and Management of Authorities

The following operations are abstract transition rules. They distinguish rejection by the discipline, defined failure, and a permitted transition.

## 58. Transition Outcomes

Every operation has a conceptual outcome among:

```text
Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail
```

`reject` means that the static discipline does not permit the step; it is neither an implicit runtime trap nor `ub` in the elementary memory machine. `fail` is a **defined failure** leaving the state unchanged; **only `alloc` may produce it in the O1–O16 kernel**. Other kernel operations produce `ok` or `reject`. Library-abstraction operations, including `issue` (§77), may define their own `fail` cases. Where such failure is provided, static preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract.

An `ok` transition must satisfy its preconditions, apply exactly its prescribed effects, and preserve the relevant invariants. No transition fabricates a permission to make its conclusion true. Holder and anchor changes are evaluated in the **resulting state** when a rule explicitly so provides.

## 59. Implicit Preservation of Modes and Anchors

Changes in effective authority are **derived** from active authorities and their origins; no `Suspended` indicator is mutated. Access operations do not change an anchor without an explicitly authorized effect of transfer, `depend`, `store`, release, or reanchoring. Leaves becoming `Init` do so through a permitted write (`write3`, `writeShared`, `store`, including during a derived `issue`) or a transfer from a corresponding source leaf already `Init`; leaves initialized in `S3.init` are declared as such.

## 60. O1 — Derivation of an Authority

**Preconditions**

1. `source` is an active derived or root authority, and `ExercisableAt(s,source,mode)` holds; its origin chain and anchors are valid.
2. The leaves of `region` exist and belong to the footprint of `source`; `mode` does not exceed the available effective right on these leaves.
3. The addition preserves exclusivity I1: no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible with the derived right, and already-active descendants are respected.
4. The new holding frame is the live current frame. The admissible state's footprint and anchoring restrictions remain true.

**`ok` effect:** A new active authority with fresh identity, origin `source`, requested mode and footprint, and held by the current frame is added. The source remains active; its effective modes are recomputed per leaf. No storage or place anchor is created. Multiple compatible observations remain permitted. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 61. O2 — Splitting Authorities

**Preconditions**

1. `source` is active and exercisable by the current frame with sufficient modification rights over the relevant leaves.
2. Each region lies within the available, effectively modifiable footprint of the source.
3. Regions are pairwise disjoint under structural composition or contract `K.DeclaredDisjoint`, subject to obligation `DDSound(K)`; no exclusive right already distributed is overlapped.
4. Creation of the derivatives respects origins, conservation I1/I2, and validity obligations.

**`ok` effect:** An active derived `Modify` authority held by the current frame is created for each region. `source` remains active; its effective modification capability disappears only over distributed leaves and remains on undistributed leaves. Authorities are split logically: `split` performs no physical allocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

An unjustified declaration of disjointness may invalidate the proof: without `DDSound`, an accepted `split` may violate I1. Constructing zero-sized subregions is not identified with an allocation of the elementary memory machine; the case of an empty shape in `alloc` is distinct.

## 62. O3 — End of a Derived Borrow

**Preconditions**

1. `authority` is active **and derived**: an authority with no origin is rejected.
2. It is held by the current frame, or by a place `p` on which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.
3. No active descendant of the authority prevents its release; no other still-usable value may lose a required anchor.
4. If the authority is stored in its holding place, that place is exempted from the check “this authority still appears among the anchors” **only because the effect removes that anchor at the same time**. An anchor with the same identity attached by `depend` to another usable place continues to block the step.
5. Applicable abstraction contracts remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** The authority becomes inactive and can no longer be exercised. It is removed from its holding place's anchors when stored there. Effective modes of its origins are recomputed, allowing unblocked rights to return. There is no implicit deallocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

# XI. End of Use, Deallocation, and Allocation

The logical end of a value does not necessarily entail deallocation of its storage. The following operations treat initialization, ownership, and physical release separately.

## 69. O12 — Logical End of a Value's Use

**Preconditions**

1. `place` is usable and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over it.
2. No active descendant over the leaves of `place` **or storage that dies with it** is held outside the places dying with `place`, in a way that would prevent rights from returning or being invalidated.
3. No place **remaining usable after the effect** depends on an authority held by `place`, its root, or an authority that would become inactive when an owned holder dies.
4. **No leaf whose use ends, including transitively owned storage, is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). A dynamic pinning obligation must be legally removed by `unpin` before this step.

**`ok` effect:** The leaves of value `place` become `Uninit`; `place` **remains usable as a place** and may legally be reinitialized. Authorities held by `place` and dead substorages are released; dependencies of the ended value are removed; transitively owned places that cease to live are marked dead. The operation does not automatically trigger physical deallocation in the elementary memory machine: an unfreed allocation may constitute a leak, which this guarantee does not prohibit. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 70. O13 — Release of an Owned Storage Unit

**Preconditions**

1. `place` is a **root of storage owned by a value** (`OwnedRoot`), not an ordinary local directly owned by a frame and not part of an aggregate.
2. `K.Deallocable(place)` is established, and `K.FreeCompat(place,auth)` justifies deallocation authority `auth`; this identifier is opaque to the authority kernel.
3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify`; no active derivative over the footprint being freed is held outside holders that die; no surviving place is anchored to an authority of the released region or of its dead holders.
4. No leaf of the released unit is statically or dynamically pinned. Ending external use does not silently turn a still-pinned leaf into a releasable unit.

**`ok` effect:** `place` and the storage that ceases to live are marked dead; authorities of those regions, including their corresponding roots, become inactive, as do authorities whose holders die. Surviving dependencies must remain valid. Every realization of `free` must satisfy the corresponding deallocation relation of the elementary memory machine (Part III). **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 71. O14 — Allocation of a New Storage Root

**Static preconditions**

1. `shape` is a **nonempty** abstract shape, represented like the local places of `enterFrame`; an allocation of **zero physical size** may be represented by a logical one-leaf shape.
2. **All leaves of the provider** are `Init`; updates to its metadata are permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid `writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata.
3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify` over `owner`; new identities and ownership relations must respect `WF3`, `RootHeld`, and liveness restrictions.

**Outcomes**

- `reject`: a static precondition does not hold;
- `fail`: static preconditions hold, but `K.Satisfiable(provider,shape,s)` is false in the state under consideration; **no state change**;
- `ok(s')`: creation of a **new storage root** with fresh identity, owned by `owner`; its leaves start `Uninit`, its new root `Modify` authority with no origin is held by `owner`; provider metadata is updated only in accordance with its modification rights.

Allocation success depends on the provider's state: it does not constitute a right to invent physical memory. Any realization of this operation must satisfy the `AllocStep` relation defined by the rules of Sections 9 and 13.

# XII. Call Frames and Return of Authorities

Frames are execution units that receive authorities, introduce locals, and have exit rules distinct from Spec 3's value-passing conventions.
# XIII. Pinning, Statics, and External Commitments

Pinning forbids certain movements or ends of lifetime. It is not a general guarantee of content immutability.

## 74. O15 — Dynamic Pinning

**Preconditions:** `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over the relevant leaves, and the operation respects applicable pinning obligations.

**`ok` effect:** A dynamic pinning obligation is installed on the relevant leaves. While it is active, `transfer`, `endUse`, `free`, and `exitFrame` are rejected if they act on leaves it pins; removal of this obligation requires `unpin` under `K.ExternalDone`. Pinning does not make contents immutable. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 75. O16 — Removal of Dynamic Pinning

**Preconditions:** `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify`, and contract `K.ExternalDone(place)` attests that all relevant external use has ended.

**`ok` effect:** The corresponding dynamic pinning obligation ends, without itself modifying values, their initialization, or their access authorities. Static obligations are not removed by this operation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

**Associated static rule (`StaticPinnedBottom`):** Statics designated by `K.Pinned` must be places **directly** owned by the **base frame**, not merely transitively owned by a static value. This restriction ensures that they do not die when an intermediate frame exits.

# XIV. Arenas and Collective Invalidation — Reference Abstraction

An arena is a **library abstraction**, not a memory-kernel primitive. Operations O17 through O19 are **derived** from operations O1 through O16 and abstraction-specific metadata: `newArena` registers an administration without modifying the kernel; `issue` performs `split` followed by `store` (after checking availability); `reset` performs a `Modify` derivation over all storage—through `derive` or `split`—then `release`, before restoring availability. Their contract below is **normative for the standard-library arena** until Spec 10 takes responsibility for it. It authorizes neither new permissions nor an additional access machine. Arena entries (Section 46) constitute the abstract state of this administration; the guard in Section 56 belongs to its consistency contract. The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here.

## 76. O17 — Creation of an Administered Arena

**Preconditions**

1. `storage` is an existing, usable place under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It may be local, static, allocated, or a block issued by a previous arena.
2. `internal` is explicitly named by the caller, exists, is active, has own mode `Modify`, and `ExercisableAt(s,internal,Modify)` holds.
3. `internal` is **held by a place**: that place is the arena value; `footprint(internal) = footprint(storage)`.
4. **Unified administration guard (Section 56):** no **live** administrative abstraction, whether an arena or a library instance such as a handle pool, already uses this `internal` identity. The relevant registries of library administrations are consulted before registration. Two distinct identities may cover common leaves: this is not in itself grounds for rejection.
5. All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are already `Init`; construction does not initialize them implicitly.
6. Dependency, holder, storage, and administration relations respect `WF3`, I1, `AnchorOrder`, `AnchorOrderHeld`, and the expected arena invariants.

**`ok` effect:** A live entry `{storage, internal, available, issued}` is added; the initial `available` set represents the administered storage, and `issued` is initially empty. Registering the entry fabricates no place, access right, or `Init` state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

The identity of `internal`, not the index of `storage`, is the key to preventing duplication of live administrations. No global constraint requires footprints of live arenas to be pairwise disjoint.

## 77. O18 — Issuing an Arena Block

**Static preconditions**

1. The `arena` entry exists and is live; `internal` is active. `MetaRight` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value holding `internal` (Section 36). Mutation of metadata through `writeShared` alone does not satisfy this condition.
2. `region` belongs to the administered storage; `destination` is a usable **leaf** holding no active authority; the destination can legally receive the block value in mode `Modify`. The fact that `destination` is already `Init` is not in itself grounds for rejection, in accordance with O8.2.
   **Local self-blocking prevention: leaf `destination` is not in `region`, including when the region is declared available.** This condition is static and is checked before an availability `fail`.
3. Applicable **static** validity and non-escape restrictions for the destination are satisfied. The `AnchorOrder` check depending on the new anchor is performed on the **simulated resulting state**, after the availability check described in point 4; it cannot turn an unavailable issuance (`fail`) into `reject`.

**Availability and exercisability checks**

4. If static conditions hold but **at least one leaf of `region` does not belong to `available`**, the operation produces **`fail` and leaves the entire state unchanged**. The empty region is always available. An unavailable region does not permit a prior static rejection to be bypassed.
5. If the region is available, the effective mode of `internal` on that region must permit `Modify`; otherwise the outcome is `reject`.
6. The simulated result must satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` **in the resulting state**; moreover, **in that resulting state, `destination` must remain under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame**, in accordance with O8.5. Issuance into a value with a longer lifetime than a local anchor is not made valid merely by storing it in the caller.

**`ok` effect:** A block authority of fresh identity, derived from `internal` and of mode `Modify`, is issued for the region; it is held by `destination`, which receives the corresponding anchor. The leaves of the region leave `available`, and the issuance is added to `issued` with its authority. **Only leaf `destination` becomes `Init`**; no other leaf of the arena value changes initialization. Previous issuances remain intact and valid. Issuance does not automatically install anchors on third-party values: they must use their lawful dependency mechanisms.

**Outcomes:** `ok`, `fail` (region unavailable after static validation), `reject` (static rule, effective right, or anchoring not satisfied). The destination may be a leaf of the arena value itself: its initialization then constitutes **an explicit write to that destination**, not implicit initialization of the entire arena value's metadata.

## 78. O19 — Collective Arena Reset

**Preconditions**

1. The entry exists and is live. **`MetaRight(s,arena)` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value**, in accordance with Section 36. `writeShared` over metadata alone, even when legal, does not replace such exercise. `internal` and the arena's other restrictions remain valid.
2. **No active authority derived from `internal` covers a leaf of the administered storage.** A derived authority with an empty footprint does not, by itself, block `reset`.
3. No still-usable place depends, directly or transitively, on an anchor in the **strict origin subtree of `internal`** (`internal` itself is excluded). Under precondition 2 and invariant I3, this condition follows from the absence of active descendants covering the storage, and remains explicit in the abstraction contract. Validity obligations of other nested arenas remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** All **leaves** of the administered storage become available again, and the issuance list is cleared under the arena contract. No still-active derived authority covering those leaves may remain, by precondition 2; an empty-footprint derivative may remain active without designating any recycled leaf. **No leaf is made `Init` by `reset`**, including in the arena value. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

Safe reuse after `reset` requires that previous issuances **covering recycled leaves**, and the dependencies on which their validity rests, have effectively ceased preventing their reuse. Any active empty-footprint derivatives cover none of those leaves. A historically issued region does not remain permanently unavailable solely for that reason.

# XV. Transitive Dependencies, Returns, and Value Behavior

Dependent values may survive transfers and calls only if the required anchors and rights remain valid. Second-class access does not imply an arbitrary persistent reference.
## 86. Arena, Active Views, and Reset

Two disjoint issued regions may be used simultaneously with valid derived rights. `reset` is rejected while an issuance or active dependency would make recycling unsafe; after a legal end of use for all the relevant blocks, the region may be reissued. Reissuance does not permit reading a former logical value without the required initialization.

## 87. Pinning an In-Place Value

A pinned in-place leaf cannot be physically moved by `transfer`. If only an allocation owned by a value is pinned, transfer of that value may remain valid when the other conditions hold, because the owned allocation is not physically moved.

## 88. Local Self-Blocking and Indirect Cycles

An authority stored by `transfer` in a place that would then become its new holder cannot cover any leaf of that place. Likewise, `issue` cannot issue into a leaf belonging to the issued region, **or into a destination that would no longer be exercisable in `Modify` in the resulting state** (O8.5). These restrictions do not promise general freedom from authority cycles: indirect blocking compatible with safety may remain.

## 89. Handles and Persistent References

In a generation-based pool library abstraction, a handle may contain a logical pool identity, an entry identifier, and a generation. This handle is not, by itself, an access right. Safe resolution temporarily supplies authority when the pool and entry are valid; a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure. These conditions belong to the safe abstraction's contract and do not modify the authority-discipline kernel.

## 90. Global and Called Frame

104	  | uninit

181	  | some y => if hy : y.active = true then isTrue ⟨y, h, hy⟩

188	/-! ## Decidable helpers -/
189	
190	/-- Predicate on an optional value, `P y` for `some y` and `d` for `none`; used to read the
191	components of `S3` (§38). -/
192	def OptP {α : Type} (o : Option α) (P : α → Prop) (d : Prop) : Prop :=
193	  match o with
194	  | some y => P y
195	  | none => d
196	
197	/-- Decidability of `OptP` (§38). -/
198	instance {α : Type} (o : Option α) (P : α → Prop) (d : Prop) [DecidablePred P] [Decidable d] :
199	    Decidable (OptP o P d) :=
200	  match o with
201	  | some y => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (P y))
202	  | none => inferInstanceAs (Decidable d)
203	
204	/-- An index with a value is in range (§38: identities are list indices). -/
205	theorem lt_of_getElem? {α : Type} {l : List α} {i : Nat} {x : α} (h : l[i]? = some x) :
206	    i < l.length := (List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.1 h).1
